source_request: Consolidate WARPOS_ROADMAP.md and ROADMAP.md into a single canonical ROADMAP.md (the framework backlog), keeping the consumer-facing scaffold shipped only via scripts/warpos/generate-roadmap-scaffold.js. Update live-code references in promote.js, paths/gate.js, path-lint.js, and phase0-verify.js. Leave historical references in _docs/phase0/* and framework/releases/*/ frozen.
interpreted_intent: Collapse the two-file roadmap convention (ROADMAP.md scaffold + WARPOS_ROADMAP.md framework backlog) into a single canonical ROADMAP.md that holds the framework backlog. The consumer-facing scaffold continues to be generated programmatically by scripts/warpos/generate-roadmap-scaffold.js, which already writes its scaffold as an inline JS string (no source-file dependency).
user_or_business_outcome: One canonical roadmap file at repo root, no parallel naming convention to remember, no risk of the two files drifting. Downstream consumers are unaffected because promote.js already excludes ROADMAP.md from canonical→product propagation and the scaffold generator is the actual source of the consumer-shipped skeleton.

current_behavior.notes: Two files at canonical repo root: ROADMAP.md (scaffold, ~40 lines, decoration only) and WARPOS_ROADMAP.md (real framework backlog, ~516 lines). promote.js excludes both from consumer propagation. Consumers receive the scaffold only via the generate-roadmap-scaffold.js script which uses an inline JS string and never reads canonical's ROADMAP.md. Net effect today: canonical's ROADMAP.md is unused by consumers and exists only to remind canonical-repo readers about the convention.

desired_behavior: Canonical repo root has exactly one ROADMAP.md, containing the framework backlog (current contents of WARPOS_ROADMAP.md). WARPOS_ROADMAP.md no longer exists. Consumer install/update behavior is unchanged: scaffold is still produced by generate-roadmap-scaffold.js. Live-code references to WARPOS_ROADMAP.md are removed; historical references are frozen.

complexity_drivers: File rename overwriting an existing file at the destination — needs git mv after git rm to preserve history cleanly.
phase0-verify.js check rewrite is not a one-line edit — needs care to preserve the invariant intent (ROADMAP.md is excluded from propagation).
Twelve files reference WARPOS_ROADMAP — must explicitly classify each as live (update) vs historical (freeze).

minimal_safe.summary: Rename WARPOS_ROADMAP.md → ROADMAP.md (overwriting current scaffold). Update only the 4 live-code references (promote.js, paths/gate.js, path-lint.js, phase0-verify.js). Leave all _docs/phase0/* and framework/releases/* references frozen. Strip the header/footer cross-links to WARPOS_ROADMAP.md inside the new ROADMAP.md.
tradeoffs: No new header comment explaining 'this file means framework-backlog-in-canonical, scaffold-in-consumer' — relies on the generator script being self-explanatory.

recommended.summary: Minimal_safe PLUS add a short HTML comment at the top of the new ROADMAP.md clarifying: 'In canonical WarpOS this file is the framework backlog. Downstream consumers receive a clean scaffold generated by scripts/warpos/generate-roadmap-scaffold.js — promote.js excludes this file from propagation.' Also smoke-test that promote.js still works (dry-run) and that phase0-verify.js exits clean after the check rewrite.
tradeoffs: Slightly more verification work but catches phase0-verify breakage at design-time instead of release-time.

expanded.summary: Recommended PLUS: (a) audit + regenerate the scaffold template inside generate-roadmap-scaffold.js to mirror the new canonical convention; (b) add a /check:roadmap-honesty skill that verifies a consumer's ROADMAP.md isn't accidentally framework-style; (c) ship a v0.x migration script for consumers who may have an older shipped ROADMAP.md from before promote.js excluded it.
tradeoffs: (b) and (c) are speculative — no evidence any consumer is in the broken state today.
Adds a skill, a migration, and a check. Probably worth deferring unless a consumer reports drift.
